content.comment_body: Hello, I have a temperature sensor connected to an analog module of a [product_name]. The sensor operates from -10 to 70°C and outputs a 4-20mA signal. When I go online in the [product_name], the analog input shows a value range of 0 to 1000. This value is passed to a PI-block. I also want to display the temperature value on the [product_name]. Although I can read a value, it doesn't match the actual temperature—the displayed value is the PI-block input, adjusted by gain and offset. Could someone advise on the correct gain, offset, or range settings to obtain the true temperature, or suggest how to determine these parameters?
Hello, Try reviewing the attached file for guidance. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, Would it work if you first specify the sensor (4-20mA) in the PI controller, then set the min/max range (for example, -100 to +700)? Assign 1 decimal place for the displayed value. Please test this setup. Best regards, [user_name]
Thank you, [user_name], That solution works well.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are focusing on configuring analog input scaling for a temperature sensor connected to an expansion module. The main concern is correctly converting the module's raw analog value (0-1000) into an accurate temperature display, considering the sensor's current output and corresponding temperature range. Discussions include adjusting gain, offset, or directly defining input ranges within the PI-block for reliable temperature readings.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward method to display accurate temperature readings on the device by adjusting software settings for gain, offset, or measurement range.
